hero.title: The open-source AI desktop client for every model
hero.lede: AQBot is a free, open-source AI desktop client. Chat with any provider, hand tasks to agents, ground answers in your own documents, and share your models with coding tools through a local API gateway.

demo.kb_answer: Most new tickets followed the September release, mainly sign-in questions from new users [1][2]. Volume returned to normal after the onboarding guide was updated [3].

home.capabilities_title: What you can do with AQBot
home.capabilities_lede: One app covers the daily AI work that usually needs several: chatting, delegating, researching and serving models to other tools.
home.cap_chat_body: Connect OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Compare answers from several models side by side, branch conversations and keep message versions.
home.cap_agent_body: Switch a chat into Agent mode to read, edit and run code in a folder with per-action approval, or open the ACP workbench to drive Codex, Claude Agent, Gemini CLI and other ACP agents.
home.cap_tools_body: Run MCP servers over stdio, SSE or StreamableHTTP, use built-in tools such as @aqbot/fetch, and manage Skills folders for AQBot, Codex, Claude and Agents in one place.
home.cap_knowledge_body: Index private files into a local sqlite-vec knowledge base, add web search from Tavily, Exa, Zhipu or Bocha, and attach memories and files to the context.
home.cap_gateway_body: Expose configured providers as OpenAI, Claude and Gemini compatible endpoints, with gateway keys, TLS, request logs and usage stats for tools like Claude Code and Codex CLI.
home.cap_data_body: App state lives in ~/.aqbot and your files in ~/Documents/aqbot. API keys are encrypted with AES-256, and backups go to a local folder, WebDAV or S3-compatible storage.
home.gallery_lede: Screenshots from the current desktop app. Select a view to enlarge it.
home.gateway_title: Use AQBot as the backend for your coding tools
home.gateway_body: Start the gateway once and the coding tools on your machine can reach every model you already configured. Keys, routing and usage stay in one place.
home.gateway_point_1: OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Claude and Gemini native formats
home.gateway_point_2: Separate gateway keys, self-signed or custom TLS certificates
home.gateway_point_3: Request logs and token usage by key, provider and day
home.gateway_note: Replace YOUR_KEY with a key generated under API Gateway → Keys. 8080 is the default HTTP port.
home.local_body: AQBot keeps application state and user files in two predictable folders, so you can inspect, back up or move them with ordinary tools.
home.local_state: Database, encryption key, vector store and TLS files
home.local_files: Images, attachments and backups you can browse
home.local_point_1: API keys protected with AES-256 and a local master key
home.local_point_2: Backups to a local folder, WebDAV or S3-compatible storage
home.local_point_3: Import ChatGPT exports, Cherry Studio and Kelivo backups

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.lede: Short answers about what AQBot is, how it handles your data and how to set it up.

items.a: AQBot is a free, open-source desktop AI client for macOS, Windows and Linux. It combines multi-provider chat, agents, MCP tools, local knowledge bases and a local API gateway in one application, and keeps app data and user files on your computer.

Yes. AQBot is free to download and use, and its source code is published on GitHub under the AGPL-3.0 license. You pay only the model providers you choose to connect, or nothing if you run local models.

items.q: Which AI providers and models can I use?
items.a: AQBot connects to OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including local servers such as Ollama. You can set a custom Base URL, API path, headers and proxy per provider, and import providers from aqbot:// links or CC Switch.
macOS on Apple Silicon and Intel, Windows 10 and 11 on x64 and ARM64, and Linux on x64 and ARM64 through AppImage, deb and rpm packages.

items.q: Where does AQBot store my data?
items.a: Application state such as the database, encryption key and vector store lives in ~/.aqbot. Your images, attachments and backups live in ~/Documents/aqbot. API keys are encrypted with AES-256 using a local master key.

items.q: How do I use AQBot with Claude Code, Codex CLI or Gemini CLI?
items.a: Start the API gateway in AQBot and generate a gateway key. Quick Connect then writes the address and key into Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI or Cursor for you; manually, Claude Code needs ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080/v1 and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN set to the gateway key.

Yes. AQBot is an MCP client that runs Model Context Protocol servers over stdio, SSE or StreamableHTTP, and includes built-in tools such as @aqbot/fetch. The maximum number of tool-call rounds is configurable.

items.q: What is the difference between the chat Agent and the ACP workbench?
items.a: The chat Agent uses the providers you configured in AQBot to read and edit files and run commands in a folder you choose, with approval modes; that folder is the starting working directory, not a sandbox. The ACP workbench runs external agents that speak the Agent Client Protocol, such as Codex, Claude Agent, Gemini CLI, Cline and OpenCode.

items.q: Can I import my existing conversations?
items.a: Yes. AQBot imports official ChatGPT exports, Cherry Studio backups and Kelivo backups with a preview, warnings and duplicate handling. Cherry Studio and Kelivo imports can also migrate providers, API keys and attachments.
You can back up and restore manually or on a schedule to a local folder, a WebDAV server or S3-compatible storage. Local backups go to ~/Documents/aqbot/backups by default.

items.q: macOS says AQBot is damaged or cannot be verified. What should I do?
items.a: AQBot is signed with the project's own certificate rather than an Apple Developer ID. Control-click AQBot.app in Finder and choose Open, or allow it under System Settings → Privacy & Security. There is no need to turn off Gatekeeper.
Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, French, German, Spanish, Russian, Hindi and Arabic.
